Lands of today's Ukraine: exact contours, 5050 BCE to 2023

Grey outline = today's Ukraine, used only as a reference; historical borders are not Ukrainian state borders. Crimea, Donetsk and Luhansk: Ukrainian territory unlawfully occupied by Russia today.

Every shape here is a polygon traced from a source map and georeferenced with reference points, not a grid cell. The source maps draw generalised borders, so these are the maps' own borders, to within a few kilometres at best. Solid outline = political territory; dashed outline = archaeological culture, people or hand-drawn zone, which marks distributions, not borders. Up to 1795 shapes are not clipped at today's borders. From 1813 the gazetteer polities are dissolved from grid cells, lightly smoothed and clipped to today's Ukrainian border (outer edge exact, inner borders approximate). Hover a shape for its source. Frames without a traced polygon source (862–972, c. 1015, Greek colonies, Goths) are in the grid version.
